newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma govt says arrests 47 for links to unrest.
newsitem.headline: Burma govt says arrests 47 for links to unrest.

text.p: Burma's military government said on Tuesday it has arrested 47 members of the communist party and the opposition National League for Democracy (NLD) party for their involvement in recent student unrest.

Lieutenant General Khin Nyunt, Secretary One of the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), told a news conference the government had arrested 34 members of the Burma Communist Party (BCP) and 13 NLD members in the wake of student unrest earlier this month.

"We have uncovered who was behind the student unrest and other recent destructive activities in the country," Khin Nyunt told a news briefing during which the government presented a 60-page document detailing its findings of an investigation into the unrest.

"So far we have arrested 34 BCP underground agents and 13 NLD members for their involvement in creating the unrest," he said, adding that three BCP "agents" were still at large, two of whom were university students. He said nine civilians who were arrested following recent demonstrations had been released.

Nearly 2,000 university students took to the street in early December at the start of a series of the biggest anti-government demonstrations seen in Rangoon since 1988. Last week two bombs exploded at a Buddhist site in a Rangoon suburb, killing five people and wounding 17.

The government has accused the exiled students, outlawed Burmese communists and the NLD, headed by Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi, for instigating the protests. It also blamed exiled student and ethnic groups of plotting the bombings in an effort to destabilise the country.
